call_contract.description: Run a read-only call against a contract and get what it returned. Nothing is signed or sent and no gas is paid: this is how a view function such as balanceOf, totalSupply or ownerOf is read. The answer is ABI-encoded hex; a single number or address also comes back decoded.
call_contract.name: call_contract

parameters.description: The contract to call.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: The ABI-encoded function call, as hex: the four-byte selector followed by the arguments. For balanceOf that is 0x70a08231 followed by the address padded to 32 bytes.
parameters.name: data

parameters.description: Which chain to read. Ethereum Mainnet unless told otherwise. The list holds the networks most workflows use; any other network Alchemy serves can be typed in by its slug, such as 'sei-mainnet'. One key reaches every network enabled on its Alchemy app.
parameters.name: network

parameters.description: The address the call should appear to come from, for functions whose answer depends on the caller. Optional.
parameters.name: from_address

parameters.description: The block to read at: a block number, or 'latest', 'safe', 'finalized', 'earliest' or 'pending'. Leave blank for the latest block.
parameters.name: block

network.description: Network the answer came from, e.g. eth-mainnet

result.description: What the contract returned, ABI-encoded hex

result_address.description: The result read as an address, when it is one

result_integer.description: The result read as one unsigned integer, as a decimal string, when it is 32 bytes or fewer

get_event_logs.description: Read the events a contract emitted, each with its block and time: every Transfer of a token, say, or every event of one kind from any contract. Given no block range it reads the last ten blocks, which suits a workflow on a schedule. Topic 0 is the event's signature hash (which event); topics 1-3 are its indexed arguments, and an address given as one is padded the way logs store it.

value_usd.description: What the holding is worth in USD

total_value_usd.description: What everything listed is worth in USD

list_nfts_in_collection.description: List the NFTs a collection contains, in token id order, each with its name, image and traits. Page through a large collection with the page key.
list_nfts_in_collection.display_str_template: List the NFTs in collection {0} on {1}.
list_nfts_in_collection.name: list_nfts_in_collection

parameters.description: The NFT collection's contract address, for example 0xbc4ca0eda7647a8ab7c2061c2e118a18a936f13d for Bored Ape Yacht Club.
parameters.name: contract_address

parameters.description: Which chain to read. Ethereum Mainnet unless told otherwise. The list holds the networks most workflows use; any other network Alchemy serves can be typed in by its slug, such as 'sei-mainnet'. One key reaches every network enabled on its Alchemy app.
parameters.name: network

parameters.description: How many NFTs per page, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The 'page_key' a previous run of this step returned, to fetch the next page. Leave blank for the first page.
parameters.name: page_key

has_more.description: Whether another page follows this one

network.description: Network the answer came from, e.g. eth-mainnet

acquired_at.description: When the holder received it (ISO 8601), where known

balance.description: How many the holder owns (always 1 for ERC-721)

collection_slug.description: The collection's OpenSea slug, when it has one

contract_address.description: Contract of the collection the NFT belongs to

floor_price_eth.description: The collection's OpenSea floor price in ETH, if known

image_url.description: Image, served from Alchemy's cache where it has one

is_spam.description: Whether Alchemy classifies the collection as spam

last_updated_at.description: When Alchemy last refreshed the metadata (ISO 8601)

network.description: Network the answer came from, e.g. eth-mainnet

thumbnail_url.description: A smaller copy of the image

page_key.description: Pass as 'page_key' to fetch the next page; null on the last one

description: Read 100+ blockchains through Alchemy's APIs with one key: native and token balances, transactions with their fees, event logs and read-only contract calls on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon and every other EVM chain Alchemy serves; a wallet's full transfer history and its tokens across networks priced in USD; the NFTs a wallet holds, an NFT's metadata and owner, a collection's details and floor price; and current and historical token prices. Every action is read-only, so no private key is ever asked for. Setup is one field: create a free app at dashboard.alchemy.com and paste its API key.
